newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia primary 1998 budget deficit 0.43 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Russia primary 1998 budget deficit 0.43 pct of GDP.

text.p: Russia's 1998 primary budget deficit, the difference between revenues and spending excluding debt servicing, will be 0.43 percent of gross domestic product, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Tuesday.
"The president set the primary deficit at 0.5 percent of GDP in his budget address," Chubais told a news conference. "In reality (in the draft budget) it is now lower -- 0.43 percent."
Chubais gave no further details on next year's budget.

According to Economy Ministry estimates, Russia's 1998 GDP will be 2,750 trillion roubles in 1998 after 2,550-2,600 trillion roubles forecast for 1997. It also forecasts five percent inflation for the whole of 1998.
The Finance Ministry forecasts a 1998 budget deficit, including debt servicing, of 4.6 percent after 3.50 percent this year.
"The main concept (is) the federal 1998 budget will be a budget of a growing economy," Chubais said. "The budget must provide for a real (tax) relief for each Russian company."
He said a Finance Ministry meeting would look at the draft budget at the end of the week and the government would consider it at the start of next week.
The law says the draft budget must be submitted to the State Duma, the lower house of parliament, by August 25.
This year's budget was only approved in February.
